title: Basel III: international regulatory framework for banks
summary: This BIS page serves as an index to Basel III regulatory documentation, summarizing that Basel III is an internationally agreed set of measures developed by the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision in response to the 2007-09 financial crisis to strengthen bank regulation, supervision, and risk management. The page lists links to various component standards including post-crisis reforms, market risk capital requirements, liquidity coverage ratio, and net stable funding ratio. No substantive policy content or figures are present on this page itself.
key_points: Basel III comprises measures developed by the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision in response to the 2007-09 financial crisis
The framework aims to strengthen regulation, supervision, and risk management of banks
Standards are minimum requirements applying to internationally active banks
Key components include post-crisis reforms (December 2017), market risk capital requirements, Liquidity Coverage Ratio (January 2013), and Net Stable Funding Ratio (October 2014)
Post-crisis regulatory reforms were endorsed by GHOS on 7 December 2017
Market risk framework adjustments endorsed by GHOS on 14 January 2019
why_it_matters: Basel III forms the foundational regulatory architecture for global bank capital and liquidity requirements, directly affecting how banks manage risk, hold capital, and extend credit. Changes to these standards can alter bank behavior, affect credit availability, and influence systemic risk dynamics—all relevant to market structure analysis. However, this page provides no substantive content beyond navigation to source documents.
